newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil primary fiscal result seen improved in June.
newsitem.headline: Brazil primary fiscal result seen improved in June.

text.p: Brazil's consolidated public sector fiscal result is expected to have improved in June, when interest payments are not taken into account, a Central Bank official said.

Altamir Lopes, head of the bank's economics department, said the 12-month primary result, which showed a small 0.08 percent of gross domestic product surplus in May, should improve further in June because federal government spending would drop.
Lopes said that in June 1996, the federal government had to pay out part of the 13th salary, contributing in June last year to a 0.12 percent of GDP deficit for the federal government.
"Certainly June will show a better number this year," he said. "Just this (the absence of a 13th salary payment) will assure us of a good difference."
Lopes said a slight deterioration in May in the public sector's operational result, which includes interest payments, was due to falling inflation and a resulting increase in real interest rates.
Brazil's consolidated public sector posted an operational deficit of 3.47 percent of GDP in the 12 months to end-May, up from 3.39 percent the month before.
Nominal interest payments of 46.165 billion reais in the 12 months to May were slightly down at 5.62 percent of GDP from 5.67 percent of GDP in the 12 months to end-April.
But real interest payments, adjusted for inflation, rose to an equivalent of 3.56 percent of GDP in the 12 months to May from 3.39 percent of GDP the month before.
"The deflator goes down, real interest goes up," Lopes said, thus explaining away the deterioration in the operational public sector result as a statistical phenomenon.
Lopes said he stuck by the government's aim of a public sector primary surplus of 1.5 percent of GDP this year.
"The primary result is really very good," he said.
